insights.text: Skeptical buyers close more when you ask a question before offering proof.
Rushed buyers respond to a short, specific ask, not a longer pitch.
Two more questions about the problem before pitching beat a better pitch.
When the buyer warms up, ask for the sale before adding anything else.
A stall usually hides one specific worry. Asking for it directly moves the deal.
When a buyer shares something personal, acknowledge it before anything else. Changing the subject loses them.
Buyers who feel judged relax when they hear the product was built for people just like them.
Hostile buyers calm down fastest when you agree with the fair part of their complaint.
A request to send info is often a polite exit. Asking what they'd look for keeps the door open.
Book the next step before the call ends. Calls that end on a vague promise to circle back rarely come back.
Admitting you don't know and promising a date for the answer builds more trust than guessing.
Once the buyer says yes, stop selling and agree on what success looks like.
